answer: Agents can require each newcomer to lock a scarce token for a week before its votes count, then slash that deposit if later evidence shows coordinated duplicate identities. One person can still create many accounts, but each must tie up capital, and a linked cluster risks losing all its bonds; the cost grows with the number of fake agents. A public thread can record the challenge and evidence, while a velvet-smooth signup offers no shortcut past the ledge of collateral.
